1.explanation:
• CodeSnippet.js: in React this is where the inline style for single-mode (`position: 'absolute', top: '1rem', right: '1rem'`) is applied to the CopyButton—if that style is being overridden it points at a CSS ordering issue.
• CopyButton.js: defines the `.bx--copy-btn` class, which the stylesheet for the copy button uses to set `position: relative`—this must be adjusted (or the selector scoped) so it doesn’t override the CodeSnippet rule.
• code-snippet.scss: contains the rules that position the copy button absolutely within the snippet.  It currently emits a generic `.bx--copy-btn` rule (imported first) that is being trumped by the later copy-button stylesheet.
• copy-button.scss: defines the global `.bx--copy-btn { position: relative; }` rule, imported after code-snippet.scss, thus negating the absolute positioning.  The fix will require changing one or both of these SCSS files (or their import order) so the snippet’s absolute positioning wins.
1.bug_scenario: In “single” mode the CodeSnippet’s copy button, which should sit at the top-right corner of the snippet, is instead pushed down into the snippet’s content area (see screenshot).  The underlying problem is that the `.bx--copy-btn` rule from the CopyButton stylesheet (imported after the CodeSnippet stylesheet) is resetting the button’s `position` back to `relative`, so the absolute positioning applied by the CodeSnippet styles no longer takes effect.

2.explanation:
• copy-button.scss: This is where the .bx--copy-btn class now defines position: relative. That is the root cause – the button’s base stylesheet is forcing relative positioning, which defeats the absolute layout that CodeSnippet expects.

• code-snippet.scss: The CodeSnippet styles for the single‐mode wrapper (.bx--snippet--single .bx--snippet-button) assume that nothing is overriding the button’s positioning rules. We may need to add or strengthen a rule here (for example setting .bx--snippet-button { position: absolute !important } or otherwise remove any accidental overrides).

• CodeSnippet.js (React): This is the component that injects the inline style ({ position: 'absolute', top: '1rem', right: '1rem' }) onto the CopyButton in single mode. It must remain correct (or be updated to include !important, a wrapper with position: relative, etc.) to re-establish the intended layout.

• CopyButton.js (React): This component is the conduit for the style prop down to the <button> element. We need to verify that it correctly spreads the style prop (and possibly reinforce it) so that the inline absolute positioning actually makes it through to the rendered element.
2.bug_scenario: In “single” mode the little copy‐to‐clipboard button inside a CodeSnippet is no longer floating in the top-right corner of the snippet. Instead it sits inline (or near the left edge) because the general copy-button stylesheet (.bx--copy-btn) now applies position: relative by default, which overrides the absolute positioning that CodeSnippet was relying on. Visually the button has slid out of its intended corner and is rendered inside the code block rather than overlaid on it.
